# OpenSim Native Muscle Capability Readback

Evidence class: observed structural facts, provisional. F09 child #12148 corrects
the legacy `create_muscle_model_variant` boundary: the historical target muscle
names remain available as declarations, but a declaration does not construct an
OpenSim muscle, actuator, muscle state, or executable control channel.

## Native Readback Contract

The factory hashes the supplied `.osim` source, then loads that exact file with
OpenSim and initializes it when the SDK is present. It reuses
`tour_matching._native_model_inventory.observe_native_model` to obtain loaded
muscle paths, state-variable names, concrete law/options and native loaded-model
identity. The compact `NativeMuscleInventory` binds these observations to the
source digest, loaded identity digest and OpenSim runtime version. Active
actuator names, state names, control ranges and capability flags are derived
from this readback, never from the target declaration list.

If OpenSim bindings cannot be imported, the inventory is `unknown`; executable
muscle support remains unadvertised. A successful native load with no muscles
is `observed_empty`. The shipped golf humanoid is in the latter category under
OpenSim 4.6: the runtime reports zero native muscles. A synthetic one-muscle
OpenSim fixture verifies the positive mapping without changing the shipped
asset. Both observations are structural only.

The view package enables its muscle layer only when native muscle components
were observed. `GolfModelAdapter.replay_controls` validates input contracts but
does not step an OpenSim simulation; its result is named
`Controls_Validated_Not_Replayed`. Missing muscle capability is rejected before
control validation can imply a replay.

## Limits and Reproduction

This boundary does not establish complete source-resource closure, native
forward-dynamics replay, compliant-tendon execution, muscle equilibrium,
activation fidelity, contact, grip, anatomical suitability, physiology, or
capture matching. The legacy target names are not model contents. The engine
inventory keeps the required OpenSim muscle-variant row and marks its current
support unsupported for the shipped zero-muscle source; it does not remove the
required denominator or change the status of other model families.

Run the focused portable suite with:

```powershell
python -B -m pytest tests/opensim/test_golf_model_variants.py tests/opensim/test_golf_view_package.py tests/unit/engines/test_model_inventory.py -q --override-ini='addopts='
```

With the OpenSim 4.6 Python bindings installed, the same suite also executes the
one-muscle fixture and shipped-model readback tests. Without bindings, those
native checks skip and `unknown` remains distinct from observed absence. See
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F09Q-OPEN_SIM_NATIVE_MUSCLE_CAPABILITY.md`
for the source and test receipt. The engineering manual remains
`blocked-inventory-required`; these tests do not approve a calculation.
